question: In badminton singles, at the beginning of the game (0-0) and when the server's score is even, the server serves from which side of the court?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Right service court.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In badminton singles, the server always serves from the right service court when his/her score is even.**
 
• ** When the server's score is odd, he/she serves from the left service court.**
 
• This rule ensures that both players get an** equal chance to serve from both sides of the court.**
 
• The server cannot choose any service court he/she wants to serve from. The service court depends on the server's score.
 
• The server can always serve as long as he/she has not committed a fault or a let.
 
• The server serves from the left service court only when his/her score is odd.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key phrase in the question is "server's score is even." This means that the server has scored 0, 2, 4, 6, etc.
 
• In badminton doubles, the server always serves from the right service court of his/her team's side of the court. When the server's team wins a rally, the same server serves again from the alternate service court.
 
• If the server commits a fault or a let, the opponent becomes the new server and serves from the correct service court based on his/her score.
